Subject: NebulaWorks dedicated pool: follow-up & next steps

Hi Amir / Natalia,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet the NebulaWorks team. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Key pain points you shared
- Production burstiness: steady baseload ~20 req/s with short peaks up to ~120 req/s during batch jobs.
- Model footprint & memory: you mentioned running an in-house 70B variant (nimbus-v1) and looking at quantized runtimes.
- Data isolation: regulatory need to ensure tenant/ENV separation for training-adjacent workloads.
- Cost predictability: procurement wants a committed cost envelope and clear autoscale bounds.

Goals you articulated
- Dedicated/reserved pool that isolates NebulaWorks workloads from public tenants.
- P95 generation latency target in the ~120-150 ms range for interactive paths.
- Clear SLA (uptime + latency SLO) and auditability for SOC-type reviews.
- Procurement window of ~8–10 weeks for delivery.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Reserved capacity (isolated pool) in a customer-dedicated tenancy with VPC peering or private connect.
- Starter sizing: 6 x A100-80GB equivalent (we'll run a sizing sim with your model + token profile to confirm).
- Autoscale headroom: burst scaling to an additional 2–4 GPUs for short peaks; policy-driven cooldowns.
- SLA draft: 99.95% uptime + p95 latency SLOs for baseline traffic; emergency fallback to compatible lower-cost variants if saturated.

Deliverables I will share by EOD:
- Draft mutual action plan (spreadsheet): NebulaMap_Draft.xlsx (attached)
- High-level SLA summary: redwood-sla-summary.pdf (attached)
- Request for technical artifacts: model size (fp16/quantized), typical sequence length distribution, peak QPS windows, and any PII notes.

Requested next steps / asks for your team
1) Confirm procurement timeline (you mentioned 8–10 weeks) and any mandatory vendor checklist items.
2) Share the model runtime profile (binary size, KV cache behavior) and a small sample of sequence-length distribution.
3) Quick 30-min follow-up with Dylan/Stephanie to validate sizing assumptions — proposed times Wed/Thu next week.

If that aligns, I’ll get a preliminary TCO by Monday after we run a sizing sim with the details you provide.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing this.

Best,

Avery Johnson

Avery —

Thanks for the thorough write-up. Confirms everything we discussed. A few clarifications from our side that will affect sizing/TCO: 
- Baseline: roughly 20 req/s sustained during business hours (US PST).
- Peak: short bursts ~8–10 minutes that reach 100–140 req/s during nightly ingestion/feature updates. Those are latency-sensitive (aim <150ms p95).
- Model: nimbus-v1-70b, currently running in a quantized FP16/INT8 hybrid build. KV-cache length can spike to hold several hundred tokens during long-context tests.
- Procurement: timeline is mostly accurate — procurement review starts 8 weeks out, contract signature target ~10 weeks if no surprises.

We can share a profiler export and sequence-length histogram by end of day Friday. For the TCO comparison: please include both (a) reserved dedicated pool with isolated tenancy and (b) private deployment in our VPC (if there are material differences in ops or cost).

Happy to do the follow-up with Dylan/Stephanie on Thu 10:00–10:30 PT if that works for you.

— Amir

Notes:
- Given the peak profile and KV-cache spikes, A100-80GB class GPUs are sensible for initial sizing but H100s give better headroom for NVLAMB-style kernels and larger KV working sets.
- Recommended baseline config: 4 x H100-80GB + 2 x A100-80GB as a balanced reserved pool. That supports 20 req/s steady and absorbs short 120–140 req/s bursts with autoscale to +3 nodes.
- If cost is a blocker, alternative: 8 x A100-80GB with aggressive KV caching and aggressive batching for non-interactive paths. We should simulate with your real model traces to confirm.
- Network: ensure private peering and subnet-level ACLs for complete isolation. We'll also enable token-level audit logs and retention 90/365 per compliance ask.

Action items for us (tech side)
- Dylan to run a perf sim with the profiler export and return estimated p95 latency and GPU-hour TCO.
- I'll draft a short runbook for isolation + failover scenarios and include the fallback variant list.

Stephanie
